A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReID5o framework and ORBench dataset. Their text, equations, eight tables, seven figures and appendices are readable and matchable, including material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, component ablations, dataset generalization tests and human evaluation of generated drawings. Appendix Table 8 provides additional retrieval results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original retrieval experiments, ablations, generalization tests, human evaluations and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The tokenizing assembler, low-rank expert routing, feature mixer and learning objectives are retained. v2 clarifies query-feature enumeration and discloses an independent text encoder as an implementation detail; it does not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: ORBench retains the same 1,000 identities and five modalities, with unchanged source datasets and text/sketch comparison coverage. The discussion of forensic sketches, additional modalities and open-world identification introduces limitations, not new evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 6 retains CLIP, PLIP, IRRA, RDE, Meta-TF, ImageBind, UNIReID and AIO. Comparator membership in the generalization comparison, including SketchTrans, and the learning-strategy comparisons also remains unchanged. Newly cited related work is not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the 600/400 identity split, RGB gallery, 32 query sets, evaluation metrics and 60-epoch training schedule. The 40,000-sample generalization control and evaluation of 2,000 drawings by 20 evaluators are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, expert-rank, modality-complementarity and learning-strategy ablations remain identical. Dataset-quality assessments, cross-dataset generalization tests, retrieval visualizations and appendix examples are retained. The expanded limitations are discussion rather than new robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for retrieval performance. Existing distribution plots and human-rating reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 match after accounting for formatting and citation renumbering. For example, Table 6 reports ReID5o mAP values of 58.09, 75.26, 82.83 and 86.35 in both versions. Appendix Table 8 and the empirical figures retain the same results and findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged. The new discussion of idealized dataset construction is qualitative; it adds no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central OM-ReID, ORBench and ReID5o contributions remain. The conclusion modestly narrows its empirical wording: v1 explicitly claims superiority over single-modality approaches in real-world scenarios, whereas v2 states retrieval improvements and practical value without that explicit real-world performance assertion.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's existing noise, missing-modality and brief demographic caveats, Sections 2.5 and 6 explain viewed versus forensic sketches, justify the controlled benchmark and its pretraining role, and add incremental-modality and closed-set limitations. Appendix A.5 substantially expands discussion of demographic underrepresentation, annotation-induced bias and discriminatory attribute-based misuse.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly discloses the independent text encoder, and Section 3.3 explicitly identifies the four query-feature modalities and their combination traversal. Appendix A.5 adds university-setting provenance and annotation-focus details. Hyperparameters, hardware, the project URL and controlled-release terms remain unchanged; the relocated link does not establish new resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on forensic-sketch matching, CCSD and spatial cascaded clustering with weighted memory, while removing the Moon–Phillips CMC reference and Yin et al.'s multimodal-language-model survey. The forensic-sketch citation supports more precise dataset positioning; most related-work discussion is simply relocated.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Appendix A.1 to Section 5, and limitations move from Appendix A.7 to Section 6 with expansion. The conclusion and broader-impact discussion are rewritten, the Overview heading is removed, appendix sections are reordered and acknowledgments are added. Most method and experimental exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The title page gains icons and a prominent code/dataset line, Figure 2's person icon changes, and figure/table placement shifts with text reflow. The existing diagrams, plots, examples and table structures otherwise remain substantially intact; no new figure or table is added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves implementation transparency through the independent-text-encoder disclosure and develops v1's brief applicability caveats into concrete forensic, incremental-modality, open-world and bias limitations. These changes help readers reproduce and interpret the retained empirical evidence. Since v1 already acknowledged important realism limitations and the experimental evidence is unchanged, the overall gain is useful but limited.
